name: Cleveland Museum of Art — who painted it?
description: Ten paintings from the Cleveland Museum of Art's Open Access collection, matching the same images used on the /learn sample site's library dashboard. Every question is built from the museum's own catalog data, not recalled from memory.

source.name: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API
source.attribution: Cleveland Museum of Art, Open Access

items.question: Who painted "Nathaniel Hurd" (c. 1765), in the Cleveland Museum of Art?
items.explain: Copley painted it around 1765, while still working in colonial Boston.

items.question: "Stag at Sharkey's" (1909), a scene of two boxers, is by which American painter?
items.explain: Bellows was known for gritty, energetic scenes of early-1900s New York life.

items.question: "Adeline Ravoux" (1890) was painted by which artist in the last months of his life?
items.explain: Van Gogh painted this portrait in Auvers-sur-Oise in 1890, shortly before his death.

items.question: "Twilight in the Wilderness" (1860) is a landscape by which American painter?
items.explain: Church was a leading member of the Hudson River School of landscape painting.

items.question: Who painted "The Red Kerchief" (c. 1868-73), a portrait believed to show his wife?
items.explain: The sitter is thought to be Camille Monet, seen through a snow-frosted window.

items.question: "Frieze of Dancers" (c. 1895) is by which French Impressionist, famous for depicting ballet dancers?
items.explain: Degas painted and sculpted ballet dancers more than almost any other subject.

items.question: "Portrait of Tieleman Roosterman" (1634) was painted by which Dutch Golden Age artist?
items.explain: Hals was celebrated for lively, loose brushwork unusual for formal portraits of his time.

items.question: "The Biglin Brothers Turning the Stake" (1873), a rowing scene, is by which American realist?
items.explain: Eakins painted several works of competitive rowing on Philadelphia's Schuylkill River.

items.question: "Cupid and Psyche" (1817) is a Neoclassical work by which French painter?
items.explain: David was a leading Neoclassical painter and a major figure of the French Revolution era.

items.question: "Church Street El" (1920), a painting of an elevated train, is by which American Precisionist?
items.explain: Sheeler was a leading figure of Precisionism, known for crisp depictions of industry and architecture.
